headline: Majors hold above their 200-day lines while momentum stalls, but ETF outflows and swelling long leverage create friction at the rally's edge.
paragraphs: Regime is mixed and split. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses in place, a structural signal of uptrend. XRP, Doge, and ADA have broken below, marking regime divergence within the top tier itself. Over the last month, BTC is up 17.8%, ETH up 27.2%, SOL up 30.8%, yet on the week all three are negative: BTC down 6.1%, ETH down 5.4%, SOL down 9.4%. This reversal from month to week tells the story: momentum topped and is now resting. Over the last day, the entire pack is flat to slightly red, with ADA down 2.1%, XRP down 1.9%, and most others in the 0.2 to 0.8% loss range. Total market cap fell 3.88% in 24 hours to 2.59 trillion, a sharp pullback.

Momentum indicators across the board show MACD below signal line on every major asset: BTC RSI 47.7, ETH 48.7, SOL 48.0, XRP 43.3, ADA 41.5, Doge 41.9. These are all in the lower half of neutral to oversold territory, which is typical of a pullback phase within a larger uptrend, not a breakdown. BNB is the lone exception with RSI 53.2, still neutral but slightly elevated. The absence of a single MACD above signal on the core holdings says momentum has not yet reversed lower in conviction; instead, it has stalled and begun to flatten. For an uptrend to persist, that stall typically resolves by moving back above signal. That has not happened yet.

Derivatives position is crowded and expensive on the long side. BTC funding is 0.58% per 8 hours, 6.3% annualized, which is material: traders are paying 6.3% per year to hold long leverage. ETH is 0.44% per 8 hours, 4.8% annualized. XRP, despite its weaker technicals, shows 0.66% per 8 hours, 7.2% annualized, the highest among tracked names. Long-to-short ratios are bloated: BTC 1.79, ETH 2.17, SOL 2.33, XRP 3.06, Doge 4.81. That last one, Doge, is the most skewed, with longs outnumbering shorts by nearly 5 to 1. Open interest remains substantial: BTC 2.1 billion USD, ETH 1.48 billion, SOL 252 million. The liquidations snapshot across a 1 to 16 hour window shows long-side pain: ETH saw 100 liquidations worth 720 million in one hour with zero short liquidations, a one-sided flush. BTC saw 100 liquidations split 515 million longs to 33 thousand shorts. This imbalance suggests long positions are being tested; when funding stays positive and longs keep getting shaken out, the setup becomes fragile.

Flows paint contradiction. On the day of September 15, Bitcoin ETF saw a 450.4 million dollar outflow, and over the last five sessions the net is 706.6 million out. The two windows agree: traditional finance is a seller on the day and in aggregate over the week. Ethereum, by contrast, saw a 142.3 million outflow on the day but an inflow of 200 million over the five-session window, a directional flip that signals recent rebalancing into spot after a period of selling. Stablecoin float sits at 309.5 billion USD, up 1.1% over 30 days, a modest accumulation of dry powder. Whales over the last 24 hours moved 81.1 million USD net onto exchanges, specifically 242 million in Ethereum and 161 million in Bitcoin off exchanges, a contradiction within the single day: Ethereum whales are selling into spot exchanges (Coinbase saw 252 million inflow) while Bitcoin whales are withdrawing to self-custody (177 million off Coinbase institutional, 52 million off the same venue in a separate transaction). The weekly view resolves the picture: the week ending September 9 saw 601 million onto exchanges, and the week ending September 16 saw 593 million more onto exchanges. Over the previous week (Sep 2), the flow was 436 million off exchanges. The current two weeks show accumulators moving coins to exchange liquidity, which is typically done before selling or rebalancing; when paired with the flat-to-negative momentum and elevated long leverage, it reads as preparation for further downside testing rather than accumulation for a rally.

Sentiment sits at 51, Neutral, within a 30-day range of 41 to 74. The gauge is neither fearful nor greedy, a middle reading that tends to reflect equilibrium. Yet the tape itself shows tactical disagreement: crowd leverage is swollen, ETF flows are net negative for Bitcoin, and whale flows are net onto exchanges in the current window. When the crowd is long and momentum is stalled and the big accounts are moving coins to liquidity, the tape is quietly defensive even if sentiment is calm. Bitcoin dominance at 58.6% has held the majority of total cap, a stable posture, but the cohort of smaller caps is where pain is sharpest: Doge down 13.4% on the week and 72.2% from its 12-month high, ADA down 14.4% on the week and 79.3% from peak. Altseason is not present.

Watch for a reclaim of the MACD above signal line on the major pairs (BTC, ETH, SOL) as the condition that would signal momentum turning back positive. Until then, RSI below 50 and the funding rate staying above 5% annualized on Bitcoin will indicate the long position is still paying to maintain its bet. A break below the 200-day SMA on BTC or ETH would shift regime from uptrend to neutral and would require a structural reassessment. Monitor whether ETF inflows (or the absence of them) resume on the next five-session window; the one-day outflow is noise, but two weeks of outflows in a row would suggest institutional conviction is fading. The contradiction between ETH whales selling into spot and BTC whales withdrawing to self-custody is worth tracking, as it may reflect asset-specific conviction rather than a single directional bet.
